newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle active $64, up $2 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle active $64, up $2 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Wednesday were trading actively at $64.00 per cwt, up $2.00 from last week's top, feedlot sources said.
Sales started late Tuesday at $64.00 in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, with early estimates showing 20,000 to 30,000 head sold, they said.
Panhandle sales early Wednesday were about 10,000 and growing, the sources said.
Kansas sources said $64.00 bids late Tuesday were passed by most owners but cattle were selling at that price early Wednesday. No estimated volume figures were available so far.
Fed cattle prices turned higher amid firming beef prices this week and recent strength in Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures, the feedlot sources said.
Gains also were powered by outlooks for decreased numbers of market-ready cattle within the next week or two, and continuing into the fall, they said.
The ability of feedlots to remain current this summer also gave owners a stronger position from which to negotiate, cattle feeders said.
